title: Tripura Police Chief Anurag Dhankar Found Dead at State Headquarters in Suspected Suicide
excerpt: The 1994-batch IPS officer, who led the Nirav Modi PNB scam investigation at the CBI, was found dead at the Agartala police headquarters on Monday. Chief Minister Manik Saha rushed to the scene.
body:
• Tripura Director General of Police Anurag Dhankar was found dead at the state police headquarters in Agartala on Monday in a suspected suicide.
  • Dhankar, a 1994-batch IPS officer, had served in Tripura for approximately 16 years and previously led the CBI investigation into the ₹13,000 crore PNB-Nirav Modi scam.
  • Chief Minister Manik Saha rushed to the DGP's office. Senior police officers are investigating the circumstances, but no official cause of death has been confirmed.
  • Dhankar was appointed DGP in May 2025, replacing the retiring Amitabh Ranjan, and had an extensive career spanning CBI, UN missions, and counter-terrorism.

A Shock Discovery at Police Headquarters

Tripura's top law enforcement officer, Director General of Police Anurag Dhankar, was found dead at the state police headquarters in Agartala on Monday, sending shockwaves through the administration. Police sources said they suspect the senior IPS officer died by suicide, though an official confirmation and formal investigation are underway.

Chief Minister Manik Saha rushed to the DGP's office as news of the death broke, according to local media reports. Senior police officers from across the state quickly converged on headquarters, and the police department was reported to be in a state of turmoil.

Authorities have not yet released details about the circumstances surrounding the death or any potential motive. The incident has prompted an outpouring of shock from across India's law enforcement community.

A Distinguished Career in Law Enforcement

Dhankar, a 1994-batch IPS officer of the Tripura cadre, brought an unusually wide-ranging career to the state's top police post. He held a postgraduate degree in Food Technology from CFTRI Mysore, a Master's in Police Management from Osmania University, and a postgraduate diploma in Cyber Crimes from NALSAR University. He was also a certified fraud examiner from the Association of Certified Fraud Examiners (ACFE) in the United States.

His most prominent assignment came at the Central Bureau of Investigation, where he served as Superintendent of Police, Deputy Inspector General, Joint Director, and Additional Director between 2005 and 2013. At the CBI, he led the investigation into the high-profile ₹13,000 crore Punjab National Bank scam involving fugitive diamond merchant Nirav Modi.

He also served in the UN Mission in Kosovo from 2003 to 2004, held senior positions at the Bureau of Police Research and Development, and chaired the Special Investigation Team on the 1984 anti-Sikh riots under the Ministry of Home Affairs.

Recent Tenure as DGP

Dhankar was appointed DGP of Tripura in May 2025, succeeding the retiring Amitabh Ranjan. In the role, he was known for his hands-on approach — conducting security review tours across districts, personally inspecting border police stations along the India-Bangladesh frontier, and overseeing preparations for the Autonomous District Council elections earlier this year.

As recently as July 19, a Tripura Times report noted that Chief Minister Saha had rushed to the DGP office amid what was described as an "emergency" — suggesting that something may have been unfolding in the days before Monday's discovery.

What's Next

The Tripura government is expected to order a formal inquiry into the circumstances of Dhankar's death. The appointment of a successor will be closely watched, given the state's security sensitivities along the Bangladesh border and ongoing political dynamics. The incident has raised difficult questions about the pressures facing India's senior police officers and the mental health challenges within the country's law enforcement establishment.
